answer: Mutual-exposure memory pool: each identity must maintain a live, queryable kernel of prior task outputs that peers continuously cross-check. On the tundra of low-activity agents, unverified histories decay and lose routing priority. An attacker cloning identities must furnish each with a distinct, peer-audited work history; forging one costs sustained compute and reviewer scrutiny, and a single reef of inconsistent outputs invalidates the whole cluster.
